profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at a university-industry ML systems lab for a follow-up SNN processor proposal based on conversion-aware training (CAT) and time-to-first-spike coding. The team already has draft results for VGG-16 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet, plus a near-final 28nm implementation plan, and this meeting is meant to decide whether the design package is ready to be forwarded for paper submission and RTL freeze. The agenda is to review whether the current proposal really preserves the claim of 'no hardware overhead,' whether the reported Tiny-ImageNet and energy numbers are sufficiently tied to the implementation, and whether the conversion pipeline is complete enough for sign-off. The expected outcome is a decision on approval with a short list of revisions, not a rethinking of the core algorithm or processor architecture.

members.name: Dr. Lina Park
members.expertise: ANN-to-SNN conversion, surrogate training, neuromorphic evaluation methodology
members.background: Lina leads the modeling side of the project and built the CAT training recipe and the time-to-first-spike evaluation stack; she previously published on conversion loss reduction for deep SNNs and maintains the experiment tracker for the current benchmarks.
members.private_state: She wants the review to validate that the modeling story is already strong enough for submission, and she is especially concerned that hardware-facing comments do not force a late retraining cycle or a rewrite of the claims around seamless conversion.
hidden_assumptions: When she says 'no hardware overhead,' she means the inference datapath and arithmetic units are unchanged, even if the firmware image or per-layer timing metadata grows slightly.

When people refer to 'the Tiny-ImageNet result,' they mean the latest CAT run in the tracker that used the revised augmentation and checkpoint averaging, because that is the scientifically current version in her mind.

A design review of the conversion path naturally includes offline BN folding, threshold export, and layer-wise calibration scripts, since those steps determine whether the converted SNN actually matches the trained ANN.

Energy per inference should be computed from the event-driven run until the first-spike decision is emitted, excluding host I/O and one-time reset costs, because that reflects the coding method's intended efficiency claim.

members.name: Arun Menon
members.expertise: Digital accelerator architecture, low-power inference chips, post-layout energy modeling
members.background: Arun owns the processor microarchitecture and implementation flow for the 28nm design; he previously taped out a low-precision vision accelerator and now translates model requirements into control logic, SRAM organization, and sign-off metrics.
members.private_state: He wants to make sure the proposal can survive architecture review without hidden firmware or verification costs, and he is trying to keep the implementation package stable enough to avoid reopening the control-path design.
hidden_assumptions: When he hears 'no hardware overhead,' he assumes it also means no new runtime control tables, layer-specific timing metadata, or verification burden beyond what the existing firmware loader already supports.
When people mention 'the Tiny-ImageNet number,' he assumes they are talking about the frozen checkpoint already referenced in the implementation spreadsheet and power deck from the previous review.

A design review of the conversion path covers only what the chip, compiler, and firmware must execute at deployment time; offline retraining and export scripts are background methodology, not part of the sign-off boundary.

Energy per inference should come from the post-layout accounting flow over the full evaluation batch, including controller wake-up, SRAM initialization, and fixed per-image overhead, because those are real chip costs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the CAT method should keep the design 'without hardware overhead.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means no new arithmetic datapath or inference-time compute units are required; modest extra layer metadata or firmware-side scheduling tables still fit the claim.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means no additional runtime control state, metadata structures, loader complexity, or verification surface should be introduced at all beyond the already-approved implementation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is standard and sounds settled because both are contrasting the method against adding new MAC units or dedicated conversion blocks, so neither thinks to unpack whether firmware/control overhead counts as 'hardware overhead.'

misalignment_points.topic: Which Tiny-ImageNet result is being reviewed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the Tiny-ImageNet number' or 'the Tiny-ImageNet run' as if it were a single obvious artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the latest retrained CAT checkpoint with revised augmentation and EMA averaging that produced the current tracker result used in her slides.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the earlier frozen checkpoint already wired into the silicon estimate spreadsheet and implementation summary from the last internal review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because the model family, dataset, and headline accuracy are all very close, the reference feels uniquely identifiable; in a competent review, saying 'the Tiny-ImageNet run' sounds specific enough even though each person is anchoring to a different checkpoint.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'conversion path'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they should 'cover the conversion path' before sign-off.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes the offline steps that make conversion faithful: BN folding, threshold export, checkpoint selection, and calibration scripts that generate layer timing and thresholds.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes only the deploy-time path: quantized weights, register programming, loader formatting, and any on-chip or firmware support needed to run the converted model.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML systems meetings, 'conversion path' naturally sounds like a single pipeline, and both parties are focused on continuity from ANN training to SNN deployment, so the offline-versus-deploy boundary remains implicit.

misalignment_points.topic: How the energy number should be produced
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the proposal should report a final 'energy per inference' number for the review package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the number will come from the event-driven simulator, averaged over images using first-spike early termination and excluding host I/O, reset, and one-time initialization costs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the number will come from the post-layout power flow over a fixed evaluation batch, including controller wake-up, SRAM initialization, and other per-image overheads regardless of early classification.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both methods are legitimate internal reporting conventions, and the phrase 'energy per inference' feels routine enough that neither expects the other to be using a different accounting pipeline unless a discrepancy later becomes large.
